articles.title: We assume your AI agent will be prompt-injected. Here's the architecture that makes that survivable.
articles.excerpt: Most AI security messaging comes down to one promise: the model will refuse malicious instructions. No product can make that promise. A model that reads outside text can be steered by outside text. Th…
articles.body: Most AI security messaging comes down to one promise: the model will refuse malicious instructions. No product can make that promise. A model that reads outside text can be steered by outside text. That includes a customer email, a PR description, a doc a teammate pasted in, or a web page. You can make it harder. You can't make it impossible. So when we designed how AI agents work inside Cairn, we started from the opposite assumption: the agent will be prompt-injected, and it will comply completely. Then we asked a different question: what would it take for complying to change nothing? This post walks through the answer. It's three independent gates, an audit chain, and a red-team suite that runs in CI. It also covers what the design doesn't solve.

articles.title: Ubuntu / Kubuntu 26.04 — Customizing the root account
articles.excerpt: The first thing one typically does in a new Linux installation is to edit a few text files, such as /etc/fstab or /etc/hosts, in some terminal window. This is unfortunately the first bad experience wi…
articles.body: The first thing one typically does in a new Linux installation is to edit a few text files, such as /etc/fstab or /etc/hosts , in some terminal window. This is unfortunately the first bad experience with Ubuntu / Kubuntu: They broke vi in the root account! Namely, after launching vi , you can't copy&paste text while editing a file. They have installed a mouse handling that breaks copy&paste. Behind the scenes, what's happening: When you launch vi , it loads a customization file: $HOME/.vimrc if that file exists, or /etc/vim/vimrc otherwise. For the root account, there is no $HOME/.vimrc , so /etc/vim/vimrc gets loaded, and this file activates the insane mouse handling.

articles.title: Warning in the nginx log, need explanation of the request
articles.excerpt: The most common mistake with this warning is treating it as an error and raising every buffer in nginx.conf until it disappears. It isn't an error. The request worked, and nginx is just telling you it…
articles.body: The most common mistake with this warning is treating it as an error and raising every buffer in nginx.conf until it disappears. It isn't an error. The request worked, and nginx is just telling you it used the disk. If you searched "warning in the nginx log, need explanation of the request", this walks through reading the line, finding what caused it, and fixing it only where it matters. A [warn] line saying a request body or upstream response "is buffered to a temporary file" means the data was bigger than nginx's memory buffers, so nginx wrote it to disk. The request still succeeded. The request: field shows which URL caused it. Raise client_body_buffer_size or fastcgi_buffers for that location only if it happens often.

articles.body: God of War's Kratos almost went by a different name, but developers at Santa Monica Studio made too many Domino's pizza jokes. David Jaffe, the director of the original God of War trilogy, recently put out a video explaining the deep dish issue. Originally, Kratos was called “Dominus,” which Jaffe liked because it made him sound dominant and strong. Unfortunately, it also made him sound like a chain of pizza restaurants. “The people on the team started making Domino’s Pizza jokes,” Jaffe said . “Every single time someone said Dominus, someone inevitably would yell out, ‘30 minutes or free,’ or, ‘Get the door, it’s Dominus.’ “After about the 50th time, the writing was on the wall.

articles.body: Comparing the latest iPhone and Pixel devices used to be troublesome. It always boiled down to the same thing. Google worked to make Pixels a more attractive alternative to the iPhone, from a sleeker design to more intuitive software, and the results have been positive. articles.title: NASA closes the book on epic OSIRIS-REx asteroid-sampling mission: 'I am immensely proud of what we did'
articles.excerpt: NASA's OSIRIS-REx asteroid-sampling mission formally ended on Sept. 30, 2026, though scientists will continue to study the pieces of space rock it returned for decades.
articles.body: On Sept. 30, NASA formally concluded OSIRIS-REx, the historic first U.S. mission to pluck a pristine piece of an asteroid and deliver it safely back to Earth. The van-sized OSIRIS-REx spacecraft — whose name is short for Origins, Spectral Interpretation, Resource Identification, Security-Regolith Explorer — visited and sampled Bennu , an ancient space rock holding pristine remnants from the dawn of our solar system more than 4.5 billion years ago. Among those cosmic relics are raw organic building blocks , the kind that may have seeded life on Earth. "I have known this day was coming for a long time, but it is still difficult to see it arrive," OSIRIS-REx Principal Investigator Dante Lauretta, who's based at the University of Arizona, said in a post on LinkedIn .

articles.excerpt: Generative AI models run on powerful chips known as GPUs, which depend on stacks of specialized memory chips packaged with the processor. To meet growing demand for memory, Samsung is building a massi…
articles.body: _____________ THE PLACE Pyeongtaek, South Korea Generative AI models run on powerful chips known as GPUs, which depend on stacks of specialized memory chips packaged with the processor. To meet growing demand for memory, Samsung is building a massive new semiconductor manufacturing complex in Pyeongtaek, South Korea. Three fabs already operate around the clock, and a fourth is coming online. Construction of a fifth was halted during a drop in demand for memory chips in 2024 but restarted when the AI boom sent demand soaring. It’s just before noon on a Monday, and construction workers are pouring out of Samsung’s fabs in Pyeongtaek, a farming city south of Seoul where rice paddies abut a sprawling chipmaking complex.

articles.title: New 'Blade Runner 2099' trailer is a space fan's dream with sinister starships and strange exoplanets (video)
articles.excerpt: 'More human than human. That's not a slogan; it's a shackle'
articles.body: Cue the depressing rain, dark trench coats, and a dire dystopian dirge because the Blade Runner 2099 trailer is here! Cyberpunk is charging back in confident fashion with Prime Video's latest detour into the neon-drenched dystopia of humans and rogue replicants first introduced in director Sir Ridley Scott's "Blade Runner" from 1982, then revisited in Denis Villeneuve's "Blade Runner 2049." Arriving Nov. 25, 2026, " Blade Runner 2099" 's plot turns the tables as resentful artificial beings are now the ones running the show and hunting down Earth’s humans after a successful uprising against their original makers. This newest atmospheric trailer was unveiled at last week’s New York Comic-Con and has us totally jacked to re-immerse ourselves in that noirish futuristic realm.

articles.title: The X-Files Lego set is a wonderful bit of 90s sci-fi nostalgia
articles.excerpt: Brick by brick ... the truth is out there. You can now own a little piece of that with this 1,478-piece Lego set
articles.body: Millennials get a lot of flak for being overly nostalgic, but I don't think that's fair. When the modern-day world has nothing to offer us but AI slop, shrinkflation and a sad acceptance that we can't be bothered to do anything about global warming. It's easy to see why we yearn for the days of Pogs, the Backstreet Boys, and Saved by the Bell. One area that we definitely had it good in the 90s was sci-fi , when legendary shows like Star Trek: The Next Generation, Stargate SG-1, and — of course — The X-Files ruled our TV screens long before the age of streaming services . You can relive those glory days of alien conspiracies, spooky happenings and cell phones the size of a brick with the Lego Ideas The X-Files set.

articles.title: Japan launches historic MMX sample-return mission to Mars' moon Phobos (video)
articles.excerpt: Japan just launched an epic mission to Mars' moons that could make history as the first spacecraft to return to Earth from the Red Planet — and it plans to come back with samples onboard.
articles.body: Japan's groundbreaking mission to Mars is officially underway, headed to the Red Planet's mysterious moons Phobos and Deimos for a historic sample-return attempt. The Martian Moons eXploration (MMX) mission launched today (Oct. 19) from Tanegashima Space Center in Japan, riding an H3 rocket that lifted off from Pad-2 at Tanegashima's Yoshinobu Launch Complex at 3:41 p.m. EDT (1941 GMT; 4:41 a.m. local time in Japan on Oct. 20). The JAXA ( Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency )-led MMX mission is bound for Mars orbit, where it will study the planet's two moons, Phobos and Deimos.

articles.title: On this day in space! Oct. 19, 2016: Europe's ExoMars orbiter and Schiaparelli lander arrive at Mars
articles.excerpt: On Oct. 19, 2016, the European Space Agency's ExoMars orbiter and Schiaparelli arrived at Mars! Here's why it mattered.
articles.body: On Oct. 19, 2016, the European Space Agency's ExoMars mission arrived at Mars ! ExoMars 2016 consists of the Trace Gas Orbiter and the Schiaparelli lander. The orbiter and lander traveled there together and separated on Oct. 16, three days before the orbiter entered orbit around Mars , and the lander touched down on the planet's surface. But something went wrong during the lander's descent, and it crashed into the ground. Schiaparelli did not survive the accident , but the Trace Gas Orbiter is still functional. It is currently circling the planet, looking for methane and other gases in the Martian atmosphere that could be evidence for possible biological activity.

articles.body: “I think I have good news about the nature of neural networks.” With those simple words of optimism, Nick Cammarata, a researcher at the AI startup Goodfire, kicked off a 26,000-word blog post that has knocked the AI world on its head, sparking wild speculation as well as cautious (and not-so-cautious) celebration. Cammarata’s claim is that LLMs might in fact be far easier to understand—and thus to monitor and control—than people previously thought. If true (and we’ll come back to that), it’s a huge deal.
